title: Customer Success: Enterprise Request Synthesis & Technical Decomposition Template
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: provide CS and Sales a lightweight, repeatable template to aggregate enterprise feature requests, synthesize requirements, and create a first-pass technical decomposition that engineering can cost. This ticket contains the template, scoring rules, example responses, and guidance on handoff artifacts expected for a valid engineering intake. Scope: non-bug feature asks (product/behavior/ops) that require cross-team evaluation (runtime, console, billing, security). Not for simple UI tweaks or individual account configuration requests.
acceptance_criteria: CS/Sales can complete the template for an incoming enterprise ask in <= 30 minutes
Template outputs a recommended priority score (0-100) and an initial engineering estimate band (S/M/L/XL)
All required engineering handoff fields are present before creating a PM-engineering intake ticket
Pilot run with 4 enterprise accounts completed and feedback incorporated
triage_rubric: Business value (30 points): revenue impact, renewal risk, upsell potential. Guidance: map to $ or ARR influence when possible.
Customer count & replicability (20 points): single-account vs multi-account need. Repeatable features score higher.
Technical lift & risk (20 points): estimated backend work, infra changes, data sensitivity, deployment model (hosted/dedicated/private).
Compliance/privacy/security impact (15 points): PHI/PII, audit logging, KMS/HSM needs, legal/regulatory drivers.
Time sensitivity & contract obligations (10 points): SLA requirements, committed delivery in contract.
Strategic alignment (5 points): fits current roadmap themes (e.g., Dedicated, Private, Console observability).
initial_scoping_template: 1) One-line ask: <customer-friendly summary of requested capability>
2) Use case & success criteria: what does the customer expect, and how will success be measured? (metrics/SLAs)
3) Customer context: account tier, contract dates, POC status, existing usage (tokens/month, models used), related tickets
4) Acceptance & UX: expected API/console behavior, opt-in vs enabled-by-default, migration/rollback concerns
5) Data & security: data residency, encryption at rest/in-flight, KMS/HSM, audit log retention, required certifications
6) Deployment modes impacted: hosted API, dedicated capacity, private/VPC, on-prem (check all that apply)
7) Approx. SLA target requested (p99 latency, availability), and whether latency vs cost tradeoff is acceptable
8) Initial technical notes for ENG: systems likely impacted (runtime, routing, console, billing, infra), approximate change areas (code paths, db, config), and suggested owner
9) Rough estimate guidance: S (week), M (2-4 weeks), L (1-3 months), XL (multi-sprint + infra changes) — provide justification
10) Risks & blockers: dependencies on other teams, regulatory/legal signoff, customer-provided data or integrations
11) Suggested rollout plan: canary -> tenant flag -> global, and fallback options
12) Required artifacts: example prompts, sample payloads, eval prompt set, contract clauses (if applicable)
